result.proposedEntry: - [RequestFox](https://requestfox.accessisight.com/) - Free Chrome and Firefox extension that records the API calls a web app makes while you test and flags the failed, slow and duplicate ones.

research.coverageComparison: Base README already lists Requestly (generic request intercept/modify proxy) and Keploy API Test Recorder (records browser API calls and converts them into API test cases) in the same category. RequestFox overlaps on 'records API calls from the browser' but its core value is live triage during manual testing — flagging failed/slow/duplicate calls and errors hidden in 200 responses (e.g., GraphQL) or expired-token 401s — plus replay, response mocking, multi-tool collection import, and export to multiple test frameworks and a CI CLI. Keploy's entry is scoped to auto-generating tests from recorded traffic; it does not advertise live failure/duplicate/hidden-error flagging or the broader export/CLI toolset. This is close enough to be a judgment call but distinct enough on actual capability (debugging/triage vs. test-generation) to support inclusion rather than rejection as a pure duplicate.
